result:
Round 81 is planned and ready to hand to A. The decision is **CONTINUE**. I made no app-source changes and nothing was committed; the store still shows 0 changed files.

**Round 80 result:** C passed it in a real browser (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` both true). Root published it as `68383fa`, which is the starting point for round 81. Collapsing groups (SRW-17 stage 2) is now `c_pass_published` in the backlog. The fake-Bearer 403 check is still BLOCKED because the backend isn't available in the cloud. SRW-17 as a whole stays "მუშავდება" (in progress) until stage 3 passes.

**Round 81 task: SRW-17 stage 3, group Mute / Solo / Volume** (decision D-29z46)
- **C's two bugs come first:**
  - **C80-1** (`U` refused with the "drag" message when a fader was only focused) is fixed in this round as a labelled extra, X1. The order is: note which row has focus, blur it (which saves any pending volume change as one Undo entry), collapse, then put focus on the group name. This needs a narrow edit to one locked stage-2 test (the UC2 fader part, lines 574–594), and the task spells out the new assertions.
  - **C80-2** (fold-button label word order) is closed by my decision: the shipped wording becomes the agreed text. It is the same words, and the order is forced by a locked stage-1 test.
- **How group levels work:** each child track's level is its own volume times the volume of every group above it. Mute beats solo at every level. A group never sounds louder than its child at full volume, because group volume runs from 0 to 100%.
- **I chose not to build a real mixing bus.** It would have to rebuild or rewire the audio graph on every Ctrl+G, which breaks a published result from round 79: grouping tracks during playback must not restart playback. Without effects the sound is identical. The one visible difference is that a child track's meter shows the level after its group, so it drops when the group is muted. The Ableton capture doesn't say what Live does here, so this is recorded as our own choice.
- **Group header:** M, S and Volume controls. The row stays 28 px and adds no text, because locked tests depend on both. When a track or subgroup inside a group is soloed, the group's S button shows half-on (`aria-pressed="mixed"`), which the Live manual confirms.
- **Other rules:** a plain Solo click is exclusive and Ctrl/Cmd+click adds. Ungrouping drops the group's mix settings, and Undo brings them back. The export dialog's video-sound line accounts for group solo.
- **Checks:** C runs 20 rows at both 1440×900 and 1280×720, including the R17-G2/G3 export checks: group at 50% must measure 0.500 ± 0.005 of full level, and a group at 0%, or one whose outer group is muted, must be digitally silent.
- **Group pan** is not part of this request (FB-12/SRW-17 name only Mute, Solo and Volume). I logged it as a signal, not a deferral.

**After round 81:** if round 82 is planned on or after 2026-10-24, it is the regression round. Otherwise it reproduces C's observation O3: a cross-lane drag refused for overlap still keeps its sideways move. That one check decides the severity: Low if the refusal message shows on release, Medium if it doesn't.

**Architecture checkpoint:** I appended a non-blocking request for root (question 9 in `b-round-78-checkpoint-request.md`). This is the first SRW-17 round to open `ArrangementContext.tsx`, and SRW-17 reaches its feature boundary here. No refactor is scheduled.

**Advisor:** used three times. It first recommended the bus, then agreed to per-track levels once I showed the round-79 conflict. Its final review led me to fix three acceptance checks:
- the group-solo and export-dialog rows now run with the video unmuted, so they can't pass trivially;
- the header width check is at depth 1, not depth 2;
- the exclusive-solo rule now takes soloed groups into account.

I didn't consult any project subagents.
